Green anole range


Code
## Note: This code chunk is not evaluated as it requires manual interaction
## to define the green anole's range using the `mapedit` package. The resulting 
## range points are saved as an RDS file for later use.

caro_occ_data <- read.csv("raw_data/anolis_carolinensis_inat_obs.csv")

# round coordinates and remove observations with low positional accuracy
caro_occ_data <- caro_occ_data |>
  mutate(
    lat = round(latitude, 1), lon = round(longitude, 1),
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(positional_accuracy) & positional_accuracy <= 1000
  ) |>
  group_by(lon, lat) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n > 2) |>
  select(lon, lat)

# filter data to native range of green anole
caro_occ_data <- caro_occ_data |>
  filter(
    lon > -110 & lon < -70, lat > 22.5 & lat < 37.5
  )

# remove outliers based on distance to other observations
caro_occ_data$is_outlier <- apply(
  caro_occ_data[, c("lon", "lat")], 1, function(x) {
    distances <- geosphere::distm(
      x,
      caro_occ_data[, c("lon", "lat")],
      fun = distHaversine
    )
    # if there are fewer than 3 observations within 50 km, mark as outlier
    if (length(distances) > 0 && sum(distances < 50000) < 3) {
      1
    } else {
      0
    }
  }
)

# save processed occurrence data
saveRDS(caro_occ_data, "data/caro_occ_data.rds")

# transform into a spatial object
caro_occ_sf <- st_as_sf(
  caro_occ_data[caro_occ_data$is_outlier == 0, ],
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

# manually draw map around range
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
caro_range_sf <- editMap(mapview(caro_occ_sf))

# transform into a polygon object
caro_range_sf <- st_as_sf(caro_range_sf$finished)

# filter data to only include points within the continental US
caro_range_sf <- st_intersection(
  caro_range_sf,
  ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |>
    filter(admin %in% c("United States of America", "Mexico")) |>
    st_crop(xmin = -125, xmax = -65, ymin = 20, ymax = 50)
)

# change the spatial resolution of the polygon to 0.04166667 degrees (~5 km)
caro_range_sf <- st_transform(caro_range_sf, crs = 4326)

# combine into a single (multi)polygon suitable for masking other layers
caro_range_poly <- st_as_sf(caro_range_sf) |>
  st_union() |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  st_as_sf()

# save caro range
saveRDS(caro_range_poly, "data/caro_range.rds")

## Note: This code chunk is not evaluated as it requires downloading large
## datasets. The resulting ecological data is saved as an RDS file
## for later use.

# get polygon for the continental US
continental_us_polygon <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(admin %in% c("United States of America", "Mexico")) |>
  st_crop(
    xmin = min(caro_range_points$lon) - 2,
    xmax = max(caro_range_points$lon) + 2,
    ymin = min(caro_range_points$lat) - 0.5,
    ymax = max(caro_range_points$lat) + 2
  ) |>
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# download 30s rasters for tree cover, wetland and mangrove
tree_cover_rast <- geodata::landcover(
  var = "trees", path = "raw_data/landuse"
)
wetland_rast <- geodata::landcover(
  var = "wetland", path = "raw_data/landuse"
)
mangrove_rast <- geodata::landcover(
  var = "mangroves", path = "raw_data/landuse"
)
vegetation_rast <- tree_cover_rast + wetland_rast + mangrove_rast

# crop and summarize vegetation rasters
vegetation_rast_us <- terra::mask(vegetation_rast, continental_us_polygon)
vegetation_rast_us <- terra::crop(vegetation_rast_us, continental_us_polygon)
vegetation_rast_us <- terra::aggregate(vegetation_rast_us, fact = 5, fun = "mean") # nolint

# download and process elevation data
elev_rast <- geodata::elevation_global(
  res = 2.5, path = "raw_data/elevation"
)
elev_rast <- terra::mask(elev_rast, continental_us_polygon)
elev_rast <- terra::crop(elev_rast, continental_us_polygon)

# rdownload and process minimum temperature data
tmin_rast <- geodata::worldclim_global(
  var = "tmin", res = 2.5, path = "raw_data"
)
tmin_rast <- terra::mask(tmin_rast, continental_us_polygon)
tmin_rast <- terra::crop(tmin_rast, continental_us_polygon)

# read and process maximum temperature data
tmax_rast <- geodata::worldclim_global(
  var = "tmax", res = 2.5, path = "raw_data"
)
tmax_rast <- terra::mask(tmax_rast, continental_us_polygon)
tmax_rast <- terra::crop(tmax_rast, continental_us_polygon)

# match resolution of all rasters
elev_rast <- terra::resample(elev_rast, vegetation_rast_us, method = "bilinear")
tmin_rast <- terra::resample(tmin_rast, vegetation_rast_us, method = "bilinear")
tmax_rast <- terra::resample(tmax_rast, vegetation_rast_us, method = "bilinear")

# create a 1/0 presence/absence raster for the caro range
range_rast <- terra::rasterize(
  terra::vect(caro_range_poly),
  vegetation_rast_us,
  field = 1,
  background = 0
)
range_rast <- terra::mask(range_rast, continental_us_polygon)

# transform in to data frames
vegetation_df <- as.data.frame(vegetation_rast_us, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(vegetation_df) <- c("lon", "lat", "veg")
elevation_df <- as.data.frame(elev_rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(elevation_df) <- c("lon", "lat", "elevation")
tmin_df <- as.data.frame(tmin_rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(tmin_df) <- c("lon", "lat", paste0("tmin_", 1:12))
tmax_df <- as.data.frame(tmax_rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(tmax_df) <- c("lon", "lat", paste0("tmax_", 1:12))
range_df <- as.data.frame(range_rast, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(range_df) <- c("lon", "lat", "present")

# combine all df into a single one merging by lon and lat
eco_df <- merge(vegetation_df, elevation_df, by = c("lon", "lat"), all.x = TRUE)
eco_df <- merge(eco_df, tmin_df, by = c("lon", "lat"), all.x = TRUE)
eco_df <- merge(eco_df, tmax_df, by = c("lon", "lat"), all.x = TRUE)
eco_df <- merge(eco_df, range_df, by = c("lon", "lat"), all.x = TRUE)

# filter any row that has NA values for any of the columns
eco_df <- eco_df |> filter(!is.na(veg) & !is.na(elevation) & !is.na(present))

# pivot longer for temperature data
eco_df <- eco_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(starts_with("tmin_"), starts_with("tmax_")),
    names_to = c("temp_type", "month"),
    names_pattern = "(tmin|tmax)_(\\d+)",
    values_to = "temp"
  ) |>
  mutate(month = as.integer(month)) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = temp_type,
    values_from = temp
  ) |>
  unnest(cols = c(tmin, tmax))

# save final ecological data
saveRDS(eco_df, "data/eco_data.rds")



Physiological & Behavioral ThresholdsVegetation CoverMinimum Annual Temperature


In the plot below, we visualize how the green anole’s range is distributed across different temperature thresholds imposed by the physiology and behavior of the species. The thresholds are defined as follows:

Hard Threshold: Minimum annual temperature below 0°C, which is lethal for the species.
Soft Threshold: Minimum annual temperature between 0°C and 5.35°C, which is the lowest ever empirically estimated CTmin.
Behavioral Threshold: Minimum annual temperature between 5.35°C and 6.6°C, which is the temperature at which there is < 10% of observing green anoles perching at night based on our surveys.

# define physical constants
k <- 0.05 # thermal conductivity of leaf litter (W m^-1 K^-1)
rho <- 150 # bulk density of leaf litter (kg m^-3)
cp <- 2500 # specific heat capacity of leaf litter (J kg^-1 K^-1)
cc <- 0.007 # canopy cooling coefficient (W m^-2)
srh <- 0.02 # surface radiative heat flux coefficient (C / W m^-2 K^-1)
ecc <- 0.0167 # earth orbit eccentricity
spo <- 1.36 # extraterrestial solar radiation (kW m^-2)
atc <- 0.83 # atmospheric transmissivity coefficient (unitless)

# calculate derived physical constants
diff_sec <- k / (rho * cp) # thermal diffusivity of leaf litter (m^2 s^-1)
diff_hour <- diff_sec * 3600 # thermal diffusivity of leaf litter (m^2 h^-1)
omega <- 2 * pi / 24 # angular frequency of diurnal temperature cycle (rad h^-1)
damping_depth <- sqrt((2 * diff_hour) / omega) # damping depth (m)

# define list of heights and depths of interest
zs <- c(seq(-0.2, -0.01, by = 0.01), 0, 1.8, 2.2, 3)




Code
## Note: This code chunk is not evaluated as it requires significant computation time. 
## The resulting microclimate data is saved as an RDS file for later use.

eco_df <- eco_data

# define function to calculate solar radiation profile
get_solar_rad_profile <- function(lat, elev, doy, solar_noon) {
  hours <- 0:23
  elon <- (2 * pi / 365) * (doy - 80) + 2 * ecc * (sin(2 * pi / 365 * doy) - sin(2 * pi / 365 * 80)) # nolint
  dec_ang <- asin(0.3879672 * sin(elon))
  p_a <- 101.3 * exp(-elev / 8200)
  geo_lat <- lat * (pi / 180)
  sin_alt_ang <- sin(geo_lat) * sin(dec_ang) + cos(geo_lat) * cos(dec_ang) * outer(solar_noon, hours, function(s, h) cos(0.2618 * (h - s))) # nolint
  m_a <- p_a / (101.3 * (1 / sin_alt_ang))
  solar_rad <- spo * atc ^ m_a * sin_alt_ang
  solar_rad[solar_rad < 0] <- 0
  drop(solar_rad * 1000)
}

# define function to calculate air temperature profile
get_air_temp_profile <- function(tmax, tmin) {
  w <- pi / 12
  gamma <- 0.44 - 0.46 * sin(0.9 + w * (0:23)) + 0.11 * sin(0.9 + 2 * w * (0:23)) # nolint
  drop(outer(tmax, gamma) + outer(tmin, 1 - gamma))
}

# define function to correct air temperature profile from canopy cooling
correct_air_temp_profile <- function(
    air_temp_profile, cc = 0.007, solar_rad_profile, veg_cover) {
  is_vec <- is.vector(air_temp_profile)
  if (is_vec) {
    air_temp_profile  <- matrix(air_temp_profile,  nrow = 1)
    solar_rad_profile <- matrix(solar_rad_profile, nrow = 1)
  }
  result <- air_temp_profile - sweep(cc * solar_rad_profile, 1, veg_cover, "*")
  if (is_vec) drop(result) else result
}

# define function to calculate surface temperature profile
get_surf_temp_profile <- function(
    air_temp_profile, solar_rad_profile, srh = 0.02, veg_cover) {
  is_vec <- is.vector(air_temp_profile)
  if (is_vec) {
    air_temp_profile  <- matrix(air_temp_profile,  nrow = 1)
    solar_rad_profile <- matrix(solar_rad_profile, nrow = 1)
  }
  result <- air_temp_profile + sweep(srh * solar_rad_profile, 1, 1 - veg_cover, "*") # nolint
  if (is_vec) drop(result) else result
}

get_z_temp_profile <- function(
  z_list, surf_temp_profile, air_temp_profile, damping_depth, ref_height = 1.8
) {

  # check if the input profiles are vectors or matrices
  is_vec <- is.vector(surf_temp_profile)
  if (is_vec) {
    surf_temp_profile <- matrix(surf_temp_profile, nrow = 1)
    air_temp_profile  <- matrix(air_temp_profile,  nrow = 1)
  }

  # define hours and extended hours for interpolation
  hours <- 0:23
  surf_temp_mean <- rowMeans(surf_temp_profile)
  extended_hours <- c(hours - 24, hours, hours + 24)

  # calculate temperature profiles at different heights and depths
  z_temp_profiles <- lapply(z_list, function(z) {
    if (z == 0) {
      surf_temp_profile
    } else if (z == ref_height) {
      air_temp_profile
    } else if (z > 0) {
      a <- log((z + 0.01) / 0.01) / log((ref_height + 0.01) / 0.01)
      surf_temp_profile - (surf_temp_profile - air_temp_profile) * a
    } else {
      damp_ratio <- exp(-abs(z) / damping_depth)
      phase_lag <- (abs(z) / damping_depth) * (24 / (2 * pi))
      xout <- hours - phase_lag
      idx <- findInterval(xout, extended_hours)
      w <- (xout - extended_hours[idx]) / (extended_hours[idx + 1] - extended_hours[idx]) # nolint
      ext_surf <- cbind(surf_temp_profile, surf_temp_profile, surf_temp_profile)
      shifted_temp <- sweep(ext_surf[, idx],     2, 1 - w, "*") + sweep(ext_surf[, idx + 1], 2, w, "*") # nolint
      surf_temp_mean + (shifted_temp - surf_temp_mean) * damp_ratio
    }
  })

  # combine the temperature profiles into a matrix
  names(z_temp_profiles) <- z_list
  if (is_vec) z_temp_profiles <- lapply(z_temp_profiles, drop)
  z_temp_profiles

}

# get solar noon time for each point in eco_df
eco_df$solar_noon <- mapply(
  TrenchR::solar_noon,
  lon = eco_df$lon,
  doy = eco_df$month * 30 - 15
)

# calculate air temperature profile for every point in eco_df
air_temp_prof <- get_air_temp_profile(
  tmax = eco_df$tmax,
  tmin = eco_df$tmin
)

# calculate solar radiation profile for every point in eco_df
solar_rad_prof <- get_solar_rad_profile(
  lat = eco_df$lat,
  elev = eco_df$elevation,
  doy = eco_df$month * 30 - 15,
  solar_noon = eco_df$solar_noon
)

# calculate corrected air temperature profile for every point in eco_df
air_temp_prof_corrected <- correct_air_temp_profile(
  air_temp_profile = air_temp_prof,
  solar_rad_profile = solar_rad_prof,
  veg_cover = eco_df$veg
)

# calculate surface temperature profile for every point in eco_df
surf_temp_prof <- get_surf_temp_profile(
  air_temp_profile = air_temp_prof_corrected,
  solar_rad_profile = solar_rad_prof,
  veg_cover = eco_df$veg
)

# calculate temperature profiles at different heights and depths for every point in eco_df # nolint
zs_temp_profiles <- get_z_temp_profile(
  z_list = zs,
  surf_temp_profile = surf_temp_prof,
  air_temp_profile = air_temp_prof_corrected,
  damping_depth = damping_depth
)

# summarize zs temperature profiles into a data frame
microclimate_temps <- Map(
  function(z_temp, z_val) {
    data.frame(
      lon = eco_df$lon,
      lat = eco_df$lat,
      elev = eco_df$elevation,
      veg = eco_df$veg,
      presence = eco_df$present,
      z  = z_val,
      min_temp = do.call(pmin, as.data.frame(z_temp)),
      hours_below_0C   = rowSums(z_temp < 0),
      hours_below_6.8C = rowSums(z_temp < 6.8)
    )
  },
  zs_temp_profiles, zs
) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  group_by(lon, lat, elev, veg, presence, z) |>
  summarise(
    min_annual_temp   = min(min_temp),
    hours_below_0C    = sum(hours_below_0C),
    hours_below_ctmin = sum(hours_below_6.8C),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Function to transform minimum annual temperatures into body temperatures
get_body_temp <- function(ambient_t, mass, in_litter) {

  # Define physical constants
  sigma <- 5.670374e-8       # Stefan-Boltzmann constant (W m^-2 K^-4)
  lizard_emissivity <- 0.95  # Longwave emissivity of reptile skin
  sky_emissivity <- 0.75     # Longwave emissivity of the night sky
  wind_speed <- 0.1          # Wind speed in m/s
  f_sky <- 0.5               # Sky view factor above ground (50%)
  f_ground <- 0.5            # Ground view factor above ground (50%)
  convection_ground <- 2.5   # Conductive/convective transfer from ground

  # Convert ambient temp to Kelvin
  ambient_t_k <- ground_t_k <- ambient_t + 273.15

  # Characteristic length of lizard (meters), mass converted from grams to kg
  l <- 0.02 * (mass / 1000)^(1 / 3)

  # Heat transfer conductances

  # Forced convection coefficient
  forced_convection <- 10.3 * (wind_speed^0.6) / (l^0.4)

  # Free convection baseline
  free_convection <- 3.5 * (1 / l)^0.25

  # Total convective heat transfer coefficient
  total_convection <- pmax(forced_convection, free_convection)

  # Radiative heat transfer coefficient
  rad_heat_transfer <- 4 * lizard_emissivity * sigma * (ambient_t_k^3)

  # Night sky radiative temperature (Kelvin)
  sky_t_k <- (sky_emissivity)^0.25 * ambient_t_k

  # Equivalent radiant temperature (°C)
  radiant_t_k <- (f_sky * (sky_t_k^4) + f_ground * (ground_t_k^4))^0.25
  radiant_t <- radiant_t_k - 273.15

  # Operative temperature equilibrium above ground (°C)
  a <- (
    total_convection * ambient_t +
    convection_ground * ambient_t +
    rad_heat_transfer * radiant_t
  )
  b <- total_convection + convection_ground + rad_heat_transfer
  
  # Weighted average (division, not addition)
  op_t <- a / b

  ifelse(in_litter, ambient_t, op_t)

}

# add minimum annual body temp
microclimate_temps$min_annual_tb <- get_body_temp(
  in_litter = ifelse(microclimate_temps$z < 0, TRUE, FALSE),
  ambient_t = microclimate_temps$min_annual_temp,
  mass = 3.4
)

# save zs_temp_profiles
saveRDS(microclimate_temps, "data/microclimate_temps.rds")

Overview
The goal of this analysis is to estimate the threshold temperature at which Green Anoles (Anolis carolinensis) retreat to the leaf litter and are no longer observed in the tree canopy. To determine this threshold, we will combine field survey and iButton-based temperature data and later statistically analyze the relationship between temperature and both presence and abundance of Green Anoles.

Latitudinal gradient in green anole CTmin
Below we demonstrate how the critical thermal minimum (CTmin) of green anoles decreases with latitude but not as fast as the minimum annual temperatures (BIO6) across the same latitudinal gradient. This demonstrates that green anoles live beyond their physiological thermal limits in the vast majority of their range, especially closer to the poleward range edge.

The dataset structure is as follows:

In survey, each row corresponds to a unique lizard observation. Some rows are left completely as NA indicating that no lizards were observed during that survey. It contains the following columns:

year: numeric year of the survey.
doy: numeric day of year of the survey.
mod: numeric minute of the day in which each observation occured.
air_temp: numeric air temperature in degrees Celsius at the time of the observation.
body_temp: numeric body temperature of the lizard in degrees Celsius at the time of the observation.
start_mod & end_mod: numeric start and end time of the survey in minutes since midnight
n_participants: numeric number of participants in the survey.

In ibutton, each row corresponds to a unique temperature observation from an iButton data logger. It contains the following columns:

location: character location where the iButton was deployed. Each value corresponds to a unique city including ATL, GNV, MIA, ORL, PSL.
id: numeric unique identifier for each iButton within each location.
year, doy, mod: same as in survey.
microhabitat: character microhabitat in which the iButton was deployed including leaflitter, branch.


Next we filter the iButton data to match the survey data and combine the two datasets. The resulting dataset contains the mean temperature for each microhabitat during each survey. In this case, we only use data from ATL to match the survey data, but we will use the complete dataset for other analyses.



Code for Processing Survey and iButton Data

# filter iButton data to match survey data
ibutton_survey <- ibutton |>
  filter(location == "ATL") |>
  mutate(year = year + 2000) |> # resolve year formatting issue
  filter(year >= min(survey$year) & year <= max(survey$year)) |>
  filter(paste(year, doy) %in% paste(survey$year, survey$doy)) |>
  left_join(
    survey |>
      select(year, doy, start_mod, end_mod) |>
      unique(),
    by = c("year", "doy")
  ) |>
  # one survey went past midnight, so we cap end_mod at 1440 (24 hours)
  mutate(end_mod = ifelse(end_mod > 1440, 1440, end_mod)) |>
  filter(mod >= start_mod & mod <= end_mod) |>
  group_by(year, doy, microhabitat) |>
  filter(temp > -9) |> # remove erroneous iButton readings
  summarise(
    mean_temp = mean(temp, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = microhabitat,
    values_from = mean_temp
  ) |>
  rename(
    branch_temp = branch,
    litter_temp = leaflitter
  )

# combine survey and iButton data
survey_ibutton <- survey |> left_join(ibutton_survey, by = c("year", "doy"))

CTmin does not scale with climate
Below we demonstrate how the critical thermal minimum (CTmin) of green anoles does not scale with climatic cooling. We do this by comparing empirical CTmin data with the minimum annual temperatures across a latitudinal gradient spanning the range of the green anole.
We collected the CTmin data from 7 locations across the range of A. carolinensis. We measured CTmin by {Insert protocol details}. We also extracted the minimum temperature of the coldest month (BIO6) from WorldClim and obtained the average, minimum and maximum BIO6 values for each 0.1° latitude band across the range of the green anole.

Below we combine data on the CTmin and elevational limits of globally distributed lizards to find the total area and proportion of each species’ range that is below their CTmin and below 0°C. We also calculate the maximum latitude at which each species can occur above their CTmin and above 0°C.


Code
## Note: This code chunk is not evaluated as it takes a long time to run.
## The same code can be run locally to reproduce the results and the output
## is stored in the `data/lizard_climatic_overfilling.rds` file.

# read in global BIO6 tif
bio6 <- terra::rast("raw_data/bio_6.tif")
elev <- terra::rast("raw_data/elev.tif")
ranges <- readRDS("raw_data/ranges_vector.rds")

# filter ranges to only include lizard species with CTmin data
ctmin_lizards_ranges <- ranges[ranges$TaxonID %in% ctmin_lizards$gard_id, ]

# define function to conver lat-lon degree cell to km^2
deg_to_area <- function(lat, delta_lat = 2.5 / 60, delta_lon = 2.5 / 60) {
  
  # unit conversions
  lat_rad <- lat * pi / 180 # convert to radians

  # define constants
  equat_radius <- 6378.1370 # equatorial radius
  polar_radius <- 6356.7523142 # polar radius
  flat_factor <- 1 / 298.257223563 # flattening factor

  # radius curvature in the meridian
  e_sq <- (equat_radius^2 - polar_radius^2) / equat_radius^2
  denominator <- (1 - e_sq * sin(lat_rad)^2)^(1.5)
  m <- (equat_radius * (1 - e_sq)) / denominator

  # set length of 1 degree latitude in km
  km_per_degree_lat <- m * (pi / 180)
  lat_dist <- km_per_degree_lat * delta_lat

  # Calculate distance of 1 degree longitude along the parallel
  dist_km <- (pi / 180) * equat_radius * cos(lat_rad) / sqrt(1 - (2 * flat_factor - flat_factor^2) * sin(lat_rad)^2) # nolint
  lon_dist <- delta_lon * dist_km

  # Return cell area in km^2
  lat_dist * lon_dist
}

# define results list to extract data
results_list <- vector("list", nrow(ctmin_lizards))

for (i in seq_along(ctmin_lizards$gard_id)) {

  # get species range and ctmin
  range <- ctmin_lizards_ranges[ctmin_lizards_ranges$TaxonID == ctmin_lizards$gard_id[i], ] # nolint
  ctmin <- ctmin_lizards$ctmin[i]
  min_elev <- ctmin_lizards$min_elev[i]
  max_elev <- ctmin_lizards$max_elev[i]

  # crop BIO6 and elevation rasters to species range
  bio6_crop <- terra::crop(terra::mask(bio6, range), range)
  elev_crop <- terra::crop(terra::mask(elev, range), range)

  # filter all areas within range and within elevation limits
  valid_cells <- which(
    !is.na(bio6_crop[]) &
      !is.na(elev_crop[]) &
      elev_crop[] >= min_elev &
      elev_crop[] <= max_elev
  )

  # filter valid cells in BIo6 raster
  bio6_crop_filtered <- bio6_crop[valid_cells]
  bio6_crop_filtered <- bio6_crop_filtered$bio_6

  # extract coordinates of valid cells
  coords <- terra::xyFromCell(bio6_crop, valid_cells)[, "y"]
  dist <- deg_to_area(abs(coords))

  # get metrics
  total_area <- sum(dist)
  below_ctmin_area <- sum(dist[bio6_crop_filtered < ctmin])
  below_0_area <- sum(dist[bio6_crop_filtered < 0])
  below_ctmin_prop <- below_ctmin_area / total_area
  below_0_prop <- below_0_area / total_area
  max_lat_above_ctmin <- ifelse(
    below_ctmin_area %in% c(0, 1),
    NA,
    max(abs(coords[bio6_crop_filtered >= ctmin]), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  max_lat_above_0 <- ifelse(
    below_0_area %in% c(0, 1),
    NA,
    max(abs(coords[bio6_crop_filtered >= 0]), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  # store results in list
  results_list[[i]] <- data.frame(
    family = ctmin_lizards$family[i],
    genus = ctmin_lizards$genus[i],
    species = ctmin_lizards$species[i],
    ctmin = ctmin,
    substrate = ctmin_lizards$substrate_type[i],
    min_lat = min(abs(terra::ext(range)[3:4])),
    max_lat = max(abs(terra::ext(range)[3:4])),
    total_area = total_area,
    below_ctmin_area = below_ctmin_area,
    below_0_area = below_0_area,
    below_ctmin_prop = below_ctmin_prop,
    below_0_prop = below_0_prop,
    max_lat_above_ctmin = max_lat_above_ctmin,
    max_lat_above_0 = max_lat_above_0
  )

  # clear up memory
  rm(
    range, ctmin, min_elev, max_elev, bio6_crop, elev_crop,
    valid_cells, bio6_crop_filtered, coords, dist,
    total_area, below_ctmin_area, below_0_area, below_ctmin_prop,
    below_0_prop, max_lat_above_ctmin, max_lat_above_0
  )
  terra::tmpFiles(remove = TRUE)
  gc()

  # print progress
  cat("Processed species", i, "of", nrow(ctmin_lizards), "\n")

}

# define function to get a Z-score for an observation relative to a group
get_z_score <- function(x, group) {
  (x - mean(group, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(group, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# get Z-scores of A. carolinensis with respect to other groups

  var = c(

    "below_ctmin_area",
